headline: Media Mogul Discovers 'Living On Rental Income' Actually Means Renting Out His Own Spare Kidney Space To Tenants
body:
Q: Sir, after reports emerged about your pivot to a 'landlord-first' lifestyle, many are curious: how are you finding the transition from media empire management to property management?

A: It’s been a logistical revelation, really. I realized that my most underutilized asset wasn't a studio or a satellite, but the absolute vacancy behind my own ribs. I’ve successfully partitioned my upper torso into two luxury studio apartments, which currently house a very quiet IT consultant and a bonsai enthusiast.

Q: Are there any specific challenges to living with your tenants literally integrated into your anatomy?

A: The main issue is the noise insulation. When the tenant in my left lung decides to play loud podcast interviews at 2 AM, I find myself involuntarily nodding along. Also, the rental agreement specifies 'no heavy furniture,' so I’ve had to be very strict about what they move into the thoracic cavity.

Q: Does this provide the level of passive income you were hoping for?

A: Absolutely. I charge a premium for the central air conditioning, which is just me breathing deeply during a jog. It’s a sustainable model. I’m currently looking into converting my appendix into a storage unit for a nearby bookstore chain.
caption: Efficiency is key in the new economy. Who needs a house when you have perfectly good internal organs to lease out? #PassiveIncome #RealEstate #StartupLife #SideHustle (satire)
igHook: Would you ever consider renting out your own body parts for some extra cash?
imagePrompt: A medium shot of a well-dressed, middle-aged businessman standing in a modern, minimalist office space, holding a clipboard and looking thoughtfully at a blueprint of a human torso.

sourceHeadline.title: Sold house, personal assets, now living on rental income: Zee founder Subhash Chandra reveals his finances

It maintains a deadpan tone throughout and creates a concrete, absurd mental image of an IT consultant living in a lung, effectively avoiding the 'AI slop' filler felt elsewhere.
